senses.gloss: m. (an adapt. of πρόσωπον, as if it were פרץ אף) face, visage, front.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 16:3">Yeb. XVI, 3</cite> <he>פ׳ פנים</he> the full face, v. <cite ref="H00301"><he>חוֹטָם</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Yevamot 120a:10">Ib. 120ᵃ</cite> <he>פ׳ פנים ולא פדחת</he> if the face is left, but without the forehead.

<cite ref="Berakhot 61a:7">Ber. 61ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>הצלע</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 2:22">Gen. II, 22</cite>) <he>חד אמר פ׳</he> one says, it means one of the two faces of Adam (v. <cite ref="D00682"><he>דִּיפְּרוֹסוֹף</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 103b:7">Snh. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>בתחלה … פ׳ אחד וכ׳</he> first he made it (the idol) with one face, and afterwards with four.

Yoma 72ᵇ רוקם פ׳ אחד וכ׳ by roḳem (Ex. XXVIII, 39) needlework is meant and therefore one front (design on one side), by ḥoshebh (ib. 15) embroidery is meant and therefore two fronts (designs on both sides); a. fr.—Pl. פַּרְצוּפִים, פַּרְצוּפִין, פַּרְצוּפוֹת.
<cite ref="Exodus 28:39">Ib.</cite> <he>שני פ׳</he>; <cite ref="Tosefta Shekalim 3:14">Tosef. Shek. III, 14</cite> <he>שתי פ׳</he> (fem.).
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 42b:14">Ab. Zar. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>כל הפ׳ מותרין וכ׳</he> you are permitted to sculpture all faces except the human face.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 12a:9">Ib. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>פ׳ המקלחין מים וכ׳</he> sculptures of human faces which throw forth water in the large cities (fountains). Y. ib. III, 42ᶜ bot. <he>היו חותמין בפַרְסוֹפוֹת</he> used seals on which human faces were engraven.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 12a:9">Ib.</cite> <he>כל פרס׳ היו בירושלם וכ׳</he> all kinds of statuary existed in Jerusalem except human faces.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 4:9:4">Y. Snh. IV, 22ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>שינה פַּרְצוֹפוֹתֵיהֶן</he> the Lord made the faces of men to differ from one another; a. fr.
